title: How to Choose a Disposable Vape: 7 Things to Check First
summary: Puff count, battery, flavor, strength and price all matter. Here is a simple checklist adult buyers can use to pick the right disposable vape.
body:
Disposable vapes are sold fully charged and pre-filled, which makes them the easiest way into vaping for adults. They are also the category with the widest spread in quality and price, so a few minutes of checking pays off.

## 1. Puff count versus how you vape
Puff counts on the box are manufacturer estimates. A 5,000-puff device and a 30,000-puff device can both feel the same in your hand, but the larger one holds more liquid and usually carries a bigger battery. If you vape a few times a day, a mid-range device will last weeks. Heavy daily users often prefer the higher counts because the cost per puff is lower.

## 2. Rechargeable or not
Many current devices have a USB-C port so you can top up the battery after the liquid is still going strong. Non-rechargeable models are lighter but can run out of battery before the liquid. Read the product page for a charging port before you buy. Our guide to [charging a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) explains the basics.

## 3. Flavor family
Pick the flavor style you already enjoy: fruit, mint, dessert, tobacco or a mix. Cooling versions with "ice" in the name add a menthol-type chill. Browse the full range in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/).

## 4. Nicotine strength
Most disposables are sold around 5% nicotine (50 mg/mL). Check the label for the exact strength and read our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) if you are unsure. Nicotine is addictive, and these products are for adults 21 and over.

## 5. Screen and extras
Some devices show battery and liquid levels on a small display. It is helpful, but not essential.

## 6. Price per puff
Divide the price by the puff count to compare fairly. Bulk and multi-pack deals often lower it further.

## 7. Where you buy
Buy from a retailer that verifies age, ships with adult signature and publishes clear [shipping](/shipping/) and refund terms.

faq.q: How long does a disposable vape last?
faq.a: It depends on the device and how often you use it. A higher puff count generally lasts longer, but real-world life varies with draw length and frequency.

faq.q: Can I refill a disposable vape?
faq.a: No. Disposables are designed to be used once. Refilling can damage the device and is not recommended by manufacturers.

title: Disposable vs Pod System vs Box Mod: Which Suits You?
summary: Three device types, three trade-offs. Compare cost, effort, flavor control and portability to decide between a disposable, a pod kit and a box mod.
body:
Vape hardware falls into three broad groups. Each solves a different problem, and the right choice depends on how much effort and money you want to put in.

## Disposables: zero upkeep
A disposable comes ready to use. There is nothing to fill, no coil to change and no settings. You use it until it is empty, then recycle it where local rules allow. The trade-off is a higher long-term cost and less flavor choice per device. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) if convenience is your priority.

## Pod systems: the middle ground
A pod system uses a rechargeable battery with a replaceable pod. You can pick closed pods that arrive pre-filled or refillable pods you fill with your own e-liquid. Running costs are lower than disposables once you buy a few bottles, and you control flavor and strength. Our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) include several starter pod systems.

## Box mods: maximum control
Box mods have larger batteries, adjustable wattage and airflow, and use refillable tanks with replaceable coils. They suit people who like to tune the experience and are comfortable learning about coils and battery handling. They are the most involved option, and our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) is a good starting point.

## Quick comparison
- **Cost to start:** disposable lowest, box mod highest.
- **Cost over time:** disposable highest, pod and mod lower.
- **Effort:** disposable none, pod low, mod moderate.
- **Flavor choice:** disposable limited, pod and mod unlimited.

## Which should you pick?
If you want to try vaping with no learning curve, start with a disposable. If you vape daily and want to cut costs, move to a pod system. If you enjoy tinkering, a box mod is rewarding. All of these are for adults 21+.

faq.q: Is a pod system cheaper than disposables?
faq.a: Usually, after the first purchase. You buy a device once and then pay for e-liquid and the occasional replacement pod or coil.

faq.q: Do I need experience for a box mod?
faq.a: It helps. Beginners are usually better served by a pod system and can move to a box mod later.

title: Puff Counts Explained: What 5K, 20K and 50K Really Mean
summary: A disposable's puff count is an estimate, not a promise. Learn how it is calculated and how to compare devices by real value.
body:
You will see numbers like 5K, 20K, 30K or 50K on nearly every disposable vape. These are puff counts, and they are the first thing many buyers compare. They are useful, but only if you know what they represent.

## What a puff count is
A puff count is the manufacturer's estimate of how many draws the device can deliver. It is usually based on a standard draw of about two to three seconds under test conditions. Real life varies, so treat it as a ballpark.

## What changes your real puff count
- **Draw length:** longer pulls use more liquid and battery.
- **Airflow and power mode:** boost or high-power modes drain the battery faster.
- **Temperature and storage:** very hot or cold conditions can affect battery performance.
- **Chain use:** back-to-back pulls heat the coil and can use liquid faster.

## Liquid versus battery
Higher puff counts generally mean a larger liquid reservoir and a bigger battery. Rechargeable models can keep going while liquid remains, while non-rechargeable devices may stop when the battery is spent. See our guide on [rechargeable and non-rechargeable disposables](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/) for how to check.

## Comparing value
Divide the price by the puff count. A $20 device rated at 20,000 puffs costs about a tenth of a cent per puff. A $15 device rated at 5,000 puffs costs three-tenths of a cent. Bulk offers lower the figure further, as we explain in [buying vapes in bulk](/shop/disposables/).

## Which size should you buy?
Occasional users are comfortable with smaller devices. Daily users tend to save money on larger ones. Whatever you choose, remember that nicotine is addictive and these products are for adults 21 and over.

faq.q: Are puff counts accurate?
faq.a: They are estimates. Your own usage, the device settings and the environment all change how many puffs you actually get.

faq.q: Does a higher puff count mean stronger nicotine?
faq.a: No. Puff count describes capacity, while nicotine strength is listed separately on the label.

title: Nicotine Strength Guide: mg/mL, Percent and What to Pick
summary: Understand how nicotine strength is labeled, how mg/mL converts to percent, and how adults can choose a strength that matches their habits.
body:
Nicotine strength is shown in two ways: milligrams per milliliter (mg/mL) and percent. They describe the same thing, so converting between them is easy once you know the rule.

## The conversion
Divide mg/mL by 10 to get percent. 3 mg/mL is 0.3%, 20 mg/mL is 2%, and 50 mg/mL is 5%. Some labels show only one of the two, so keep the rule handy.

## Typical ranges
- **0-3 mg/mL:** common in freebase liquids used in large sub-ohm tanks.
- **6-12 mg/mL:** moderate strengths in freebase liquids.
- **20-35 mg/mL:** common range for nicotine salts used in pod devices.
- **50 mg/mL (5%):** typical for many disposable vapes and high-strength salts.

## Salts versus freebase
Nicotine salts feel smoother at higher strengths, which is why pods and disposables use them. Freebase is harsher at the same level, so it is usually sold at lower strengths. Our comparison of [nicotine salts and freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) goes deeper.

## How adults choose a strength
Match the device first. Low-power pod systems pair with salts, while high-power tanks pair with lower-strength freebase. Beyond that, strength is personal. Many adults who use nicotine regularly start at a mid-range salt and adjust over time. Our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range lists strength on every product page.

## Important reminders
Nicotine is addictive. These products are for adults 21 and over, are not for use by anyone pregnant or nursing, and should be kept away from children and pets. Nothing here is medical advice.

faq.q: How do I convert mg/mL to percent?
faq.a: Divide by 10. For example, 50 mg/mL equals 5%.

faq.q: Is higher strength better?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Strength is a matter of preference and device type, and a higher number is simply a higher dose per puff.

title: Nicotine Salts vs Freebase E-Liquid: Key Differences
summary: Salts and freebase deliver nicotine differently. See how they feel, which devices suit each and how to choose between them.
body:
E-liquid comes in two main nicotine types, and the difference affects how the vapor feels, which device you should use and how much you spend.

## What freebase is
Freebase nicotine is the traditional form used in e-liquid for years. At lower strengths it produces a throat hit that many people associate with a classic vape. At higher strengths it becomes harsh, which is why freebase is sold at lower strengths such as 3 to 12 mg/mL.

## What nicotine salts are
Nicotine salts pair nicotine with an acid, which changes the pH and makes the vapor feel smoother at higher strengths. That is why salts are sold from around 20 mg/mL up to 50 mg/mL and are common in pod systems and disposables.

## Which device suits which
- **Freebase:** works well in higher-wattage tanks, including sub-ohm setups with larger clouds.
- **Salts:** work best in low-power pods and small devices, where each puff is smaller but stronger.

## Cost and use
Because salts use higher strengths in small amounts, a 30 mL bottle can last a long time. Freebase is often sold in larger bottles for tanks that use more liquid. Browse both in our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range, or see compatible hardware in [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/).

## Choosing
Pick the device first, then match the liquid type. If you are unsure of your strength, read the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/). Nicotine is addictive and these products are strictly for adults 21 and over.

faq.q: Can I use salts in a sub-ohm tank?
faq.a: It is not recommended. High power with high strength can be too intense, and most salts are formulated for low-power devices.

faq.q: Do salts taste different?
faq.a: Many users find salts smoother and flavors slightly softer, but flavor ultimately depends on the recipe.

title: PG and VG Ratios Explained: How They Change Your Vape
summary: E-liquid is mostly propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin. Learn how the ratio affects throat feel, vapor and which device it suits.
body:
Almost every e-liquid is built on two liquids: propylene glycol (PG) and vegetable glycerin (VG). The ratio between them shapes how your vape feels and which hardware it works in.

## What PG does
PG is thin and carries flavor well. It gives a crisper throat feel and lets liquid wick quickly through small coils. Higher-PG liquids suit pod systems and starter kits.

## What VG does
VG is thicker and slightly sweet. It produces denser vapor and a smoother feel. Higher-VG liquids suit sub-ohm tanks with large coils and generous airflow.

## Common ratios
- **50/50:** a balanced blend that works in most pods and mouth-to-lung devices.
- **60/40 or 70/30 PG-heavy:** very thin, best for small pods.
- **70/30 VG-heavy:** thicker, intended for sub-ohm tanks.
- **Max VG:** the thickest option, only suitable for hardware designed for it.

## Match ratio to hardware
A thick liquid in a small pod can fail to wick and cause a burnt taste. A thin liquid in a powerful tank can leak. Check the hardware recommendation before buying. Our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) descriptions list what each device is built for, and the guide on [troubleshooting a burnt taste](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/) explains what happens when they are mismatched.

## Allergies and sensitivities
Some people react to PG or VG. If you notice irritation, stop using the product and talk to a healthcare professional. Nicotine is addictive and products are for adults 21 and over.

faq.q: Which is better, PG or VG?
faq.a: Neither is better overall. PG favors flavor and throat feel, VG favors vapor density. Choose based on your device.

faq.q: What ratio are disposables?
faq.a: Disposable liquid ratios are usually set by the manufacturer and are not always listed. They are tuned to the built-in coil.

title: Your First Vape Kit: A Plain-English Buyer's Guide
summary: Choosing a starter kit as an adult? Here is what is in the box, what to look for, and how to avoid the common beginner mistakes.
body:
A vape kit bundles everything needed to start: a battery device, a tank or pod and usually a charging cable. If you are an adult trying vaping for the first time, a kit is often a better value than a disposable.

## What comes in the box
Most starter kits include the device, one or two pods or a tank, a replacement coil and a USB cable. Some include a lanyard or case. Liquid is normally sold separately.

## Pod kit or tank kit
Pod kits are the simplest. You fill or swap a pod and press to draw or use a button. Tank kits add adjustable airflow and more power. For beginners, a pod kit is easier. Browse our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and compare sizes.

## Features that matter
- **Battery size:** measured in mAh. Larger lasts longer, but is bulkier.
- **Charging:** USB-C is faster and easier to replace than older ports.
- **Draw style:** auto-draw devices fire when you inhale; button devices fire when pressed.
- **Pod capacity:** bigger pods mean fewer refills.

## Picking a liquid
Match nicotine type to the device. Pods generally pair with nicotine salts, so look at [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) labeled for pods. Our guide to [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) explains why.

## Common beginner mistakes
- Overfilling a pod, which causes leaks.
- Not priming a new coil, which can burn it.
- Using the wrong liquid thickness.
Read [how to prime a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) before the first use. Nicotine is addictive and these products are for adults 21+.

faq.q: Do kits come with liquid?
faq.a: Usually not. Some pre-filled pod kits include a pod, but most kits require you to buy e-liquid separately.

faq.q: How long does a starter kit last?
faq.a: The device can last a long time with care. Pods and coils are consumable and are replaced every few weeks depending on use.

title: Rechargeable vs Non-Rechargeable Disposables Compared
summary: Should you buy a disposable you can recharge? Compare battery life, weight, price and waste so you pick the right type.
body:
Not every disposable vape is truly single-charge. Many modern devices include a USB-C port, and the difference changes how long you get out of the product.

## How non-rechargeable devices work
A non-rechargeable disposable ships with a battery sized to last roughly as long as the liquid inside. They are small and light, but if the battery drains early there is no fix. They tend to be cheaper and best for occasional use.

## How rechargeable devices work
A rechargeable disposable has a larger battery and a charging port. If the liquid outlasts the battery, you plug it in and carry on. That makes them suitable for heavy or daily use and for higher puff counts. See our [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) guide.

## Compare at a glance
- **Weight and size:** non-rechargeable lighter.
- **Cost:** non-rechargeable cheaper up front.
- **Life:** rechargeable usually delivers the full stated puff count.
- **Waste:** both contain a lithium battery that needs proper recycling.

## How to tell which you are buying
Product pages and packaging mention a Type-C or USB-C port when one is present. Look for it in the listing for any device in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). If the page is silent, ask support through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Disposal
Never put a battery-containing device in household trash if local rules say otherwise. See our [disposal guide](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Nicotine is addictive; adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is it okay to charge a non-rechargeable disposable?
faq.a: No. If there is no charging port, do not try to charge it by other means.

faq.q: Do rechargeable ones cost more?
faq.a: Usually slightly more, but they often give better value per puff.

title: Mesh Coils vs Standard Coils: Flavor, Heat and Lifespan
summary: Mesh coils heat more evenly than traditional wire coils. See how they compare for flavor, vapor and how long each type lasts.
body:
The coil is the heating element that turns liquid into vapor. In recent years mesh coils have become standard in many disposables and pods, and the reason is how they heat.

## Traditional wire coils
A wire coil is a wire wrapped around cotton. It heats from a small area and can create hot spots. Wire coils are simple, widely available and low-cost, and they remain common in many tanks.

## Mesh coils
A mesh coil uses a thin sheet of metal mesh with a much larger surface area touching the cotton. It heats more evenly and quickly, which usually gives smoother flavor and consistent vapor from the first puff to the last.

## How they compare
- **Flavor:** mesh often tastes cleaner and fuller.
- **Warm-up time:** mesh heats faster.
- **Lifespan:** well-matched mesh can last longer, but thick or sweet liquids shorten any coil.
- **Cost:** mesh coils are usually a little more expensive.

## Dual-mesh designs
Some devices use two mesh layers for even more surface area. They promise smooth, consistent flavor, though results still depend on liquid and battery.

## Shopping for replacements
If you are buying parts, check the exact model before ordering. Our [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) catalog lists compatibility. Care matters as much as type, so see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). Nicotine is addictive. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Do mesh coils last longer?
faq.a: They often do, but liquid type, power and care have a bigger effect than coil material.

faq.q: Can I use any coil in my tank?
faq.a: No. Coils are designed for specific tanks and pods, so always match the model.

title: What Is a Pod Vape? Open vs Closed Pods Explained
summary: Pod vapes are compact and simple. Learn the difference between open and closed pods, and how to pick one that fits your lifestyle.
body:
A pod vape is a small battery unit that uses a snap-in pod holding the liquid and coil. It is popular because it is compact, easy to use and less fiddly than a tank.

## Closed pods
Closed pods arrive pre-filled and are thrown away or recycled when empty. They are convenient and leak-resistant, but you are limited to the flavors the manufacturer sells for that device. Many [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) work this way.

## Open pods
Open pods are refillable. You fill them with your own e-liquid and replace the coil when it wears out. They cost less over time and give unlimited flavor choice, at the price of a little extra effort.

## Things to look for
- **Pod capacity:** typically 2 mL, which is the limit in many regions.
- **Coil type:** mesh coils give smoother flavor.
- **Battery:** 400 to 1,000 mAh is typical for pod devices.
- **Draw activation:** auto-draw is easy, button-fire gives more control.

## Choosing liquid
Pods pair well with nicotine salts. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) designed for them, and check our [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) guide.

## Care tips
Do not overfill, keep pods upright when storing, and let a new coil soak before the first puff. Our guide on [priming a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) covers it. Nicotine is addictive; adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Are pod vapes better than disposables?
faq.a: They suit people who vape often and want lower running costs. Disposables suit people who want zero upkeep.

faq.q: How often do pods need replacing?
faq.a: Closed pods when they are empty. Refillable pod coils typically every one to three weeks depending on use.

title: Sub-Ohm vs Mouth-to-Lung Vaping: What's the Difference?
summary: Two draw styles, two hardware setups. See how sub-ohm and mouth-to-lung differ in airflow, power, liquid choice and feel.
body:
Vaping styles are described by how you inhale. The two most common are mouth-to-lung (MTL) and sub-ohm direct-to-lung (DTL), and they require different gear.

## Mouth-to-lung
You draw vapor into your mouth first, pause, then inhale. It feels similar to drawing on a cigarette. MTL devices use tighter airflow, higher-resistance coils and lower power. This pairs well with nicotine salts and higher-PG liquids. Most pod systems and disposables are MTL.

## Direct-to-lung
You inhale directly into the lungs with a wide-open draw. Sub-ohm coils have resistance below one ohm, use more power and make more vapor. They work best with lower-strength, higher-VG freebase liquid.

## Key differences
- **Airflow:** MTL tight, DTL open.
- **Power:** MTL low, DTL high.
- **Liquid use:** DTL uses much more.
- **Nicotine strength:** MTL higher, DTL lower.

## Picking hardware
For MTL, start with a pod kit from our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). For DTL, look at box mods and sub-ohm tanks. Always match liquid to hardware; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## A caution on power
High-power devices need correctly rated batteries and careful handling. Read the manual, never mix batteries and keep devices away from heat. Nicotine is addictive; these products are for adults 21 and over.

faq.q: Which style is best for beginners?
faq.a: MTL is generally easier because the hardware is simpler and the liquid is lower volume.

faq.q: Can I do both with one device?
faq.a: Some adjustable devices support both, but they are usually designed primarily for one style.

title: How to Read an E-Liquid Label (Strength, Ratio, Warnings)
summary: Every e-liquid bottle carries the same key facts. Here is how to read bottle size, nicotine strength, PG/VG ratio and the required warning.
body:
An e-liquid label looks busy, but it follows a predictable pattern. Once you know where to look, you can compare bottles in seconds.

## Bottle size and fill
The volume appears in milliliters (mL), for example 30 mL or 100 mL. Large bottles often contain a "shortfill": less liquid than the bottle's capacity so you can add nicotine shots. Nicotine-ready bottles are filled to the top.

## Nicotine strength
Look for mg/mL or a percent. The conversion is simple: divide mg/mL by 10 to get percent. Our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) has the full table.

## PG/VG ratio
Printed as numbers such as 50/50 or 70/30, the first is usually PG and the second VG. The ratio guides which device suits the liquid; see [PG and VG explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Nicotine type
Salts and freebase are labeled differently. Salts often say "nic salt" or "salt nicotine". If it is not stated, check the product page in [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/).

## Warning statement
Labels in the United States carry a warning that the product contains nicotine and that nicotine is an addictive chemical. If a bottle lacks this, do not buy it.

## Batch and date information
Many bottles show a batch code and best-by date. Use liquid before the date, and store it away from heat and light as explained in [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/).

## Child-resistant packaging
Look for a child-resistant cap. Always keep liquids out of reach of children and pets. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: What does shortfill mean?
faq.a: A shortfill bottle contains less liquid than its capacity, leaving room to add nicotine shots yourself.

faq.q: Why is there no nicotine on my bottle?
faq.a: Some liquids are sold at 0 mg for people who want flavor without nicotine. The label will say 0 mg or 0%.

title: 30 mL, 60 mL or 100 mL? Choosing the Right E-Liquid Bottle
summary: Bottle size changes both price and how fast you use liquid. Learn when a small 30 mL makes sense and when a 100 mL bottle saves money.
body:
E-liquid bottles come in several sizes. The best one is not always the largest, and the right choice depends on strength, device and how often you vape.

## 30 mL: salts and pods
Thirty milliliters is the standard size for nicotine salts. Because salts are high strength and used in small pods, a 30 mL bottle lasts a long time. They are also easy to carry and store. Browse them in our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range.

## 60 mL: balanced shortfills
Sixty milliliter bottles are common for freebase and for shortfill recipes. They suit regular users of small to mid-size tanks.

## 100 mL: tank users
Hundred-milliliter bottles are best for sub-ohm tanks, which burn through liquid. They usually offer the lowest price per milliliter, but only if you will use it before the best-by date.

## Price per milliliter
Divide the price by the size to compare fairly. A 100 mL bottle at $12 costs about 12 cents per mL, while a 30 mL at $12 costs 40 cents. That gap makes larger sizes attractive for heavy use of low-strength liquid.

## Freshness and storage
Large bottles stay open longer, so keep them cool and dark and use a smaller refill bottle for travel. See [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) for details.

## Which should you pick?
Salts in pods: 30 mL. Freebase in small tanks: 60 mL. Freebase in large tanks: 100 mL. If you are unsure of your hardware, our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) can help. Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Is a bigger bottle always cheaper?
faq.a: Per milliliter, usually yes. But it is only a saving if you finish it before it ages.

faq.q: Can I carry a large bottle when traveling?
faq.a: Rules vary. Decant into a small bottle for convenience and check carrier rules before you travel.

title: How to Compare Vape Prices: Cost per Puff and Cost per mL
summary: A low sticker price can be poor value. Use cost per puff, cost per mL and total running cost to compare vapes fairly.
body:
Vape prices vary widely, so a simple method helps you compare. These three numbers make it easy.

## Cost per puff (disposables)
Divide the price by the stated puff count. A $17.99 device rated at 30,000 puffs costs about six-hundredths of a cent per puff. A $12.99 device rated at 5,000 puffs costs about a quarter of a cent. Higher puff counts usually win on value, though real counts vary. Read [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/) for the caveats.

## Cost per mL (e-liquid)
Divide the price by the bottle size. Larger bottles are cheaper per mL, but salts are consumed slowly because of their strength, so a 30 mL bottle may last as long as a larger freebase bottle. Compare inside [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/).

## Running cost (kits)
For a refillable kit, add up the device, the liquid you will use per week and the replacement coils or pods. A kit often costs more up front but less per month than disposables.

## Check what is included
A multi-pack, free shipping threshold or crypto and gift card discount can change the total. We offer a discount for crypto and gift card payments, and free shipping on qualifying orders. See the [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Beware false economy
The cheapest device is not a bargain if it fails early. Look at product details and brand reputation in our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) listings before you decide.

## A quick example
Two items at $18 and $24 look far apart, but if the second lasts three times longer, it costs less per puff. Always compare the full picture. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is cost per puff reliable?
faq.a: It is a useful guide, but because puff counts are estimates it should be treated as a comparison tool, not an exact figure.

faq.q: Do multi-pack deals save money?
faq.a: Often yes. Check whether the per-unit price drops enough to justify buying more than you will use soon.

title: How to Pick the Right Replacement Coil or Pod
summary: Coils and pods are not universal. Follow these steps to find the exact replacement for your device and avoid returns.
body:
Replacement coils and pods are the most common reason for a wrong-part order. They look similar, but fitments differ. Here is how to get it right the first time.

## Start with your device name
Find the exact model on the device or box, not just the brand. Many brands make a dozen pod systems that all use different pods.

## Check the series
Coil and pod listings usually name compatible devices. In our [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) category, each product states what it fits. If your device is not listed, do not guess.

## Match the resistance
Coils list a resistance in ohms. Lower resistance means more power and more vapor, higher resistance suits tighter draws. Use the resistance your device was designed for. Our guide to [sub-ohm and mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/) helps you decide.

## Pick the liquid type
Some coils suit thicker liquid and higher power, others suit thin salt-based liquid. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Buy a spare
Keep one spare on hand so a worn coil does not leave you without a working device. Learn [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Avoid counterfeit parts
Buy from a reputable seller. Poorly made coils can taste burnt or fail early.

## When you are stuck
Send us the model name and a photo through the [contact page](/contact/) and we will point you to the right part. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I use a different brand's coil in my device?
faq.a: Generally no. Fitments and wattage ranges are specific, so use only parts listed as compatible.

faq.q: How do I know a coil needs replacing?
faq.a: A burnt taste, weak flavor or gurgling are the common signs.

title: Disposable Vapes With Screens: Are They Worth It?
summary: Display disposables show battery and liquid levels. See what the screen tells you, what it costs and whether you need one.
body:
A growing number of disposables include a small display. It is a nice feature, but is it worth paying for? That depends on how you vape.

## What the screen shows
Most displays show battery level and remaining liquid. Some show puff count, the current power mode or a charging indicator. The idea is to remove guesswork about when the device is nearly empty.

## Benefits
- **No surprises:** you see when the battery or liquid is low.
- **Planning:** you can top up the battery or order a replacement in time.
- **Mode feedback:** devices with power modes show which is active.

## Drawbacks
- **Price:** devices with screens usually cost slightly more.
- **Battery draw:** the display uses a little power.
- **Failure points:** one more component that can fail.

## Who benefits most
Heavy daily users and anyone who travels often get the most value, since running out is inconvenient. Occasional users can do fine without one.

## Alternatives
Many devices without screens use an LED that blinks when the battery is low. Our guide to [indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/) explains the common patterns.

## Where to look
Filter [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) for models that mention a display in the description, and compare them using [price per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Does a screen mean a better device?
faq.a: Not automatically. It adds information, but flavor and performance depend on the coil, liquid and battery.

faq.q: Can the display be wrong?
faq.a: Liquid level on some devices is an estimate based on use, so treat it as a guide.

title: Adjustable Airflow Explained: Tighter or Looser Draw
summary: Airflow controls how easily air passes through your device. Learn how to adjust it for flavor, vapor and a comfortable draw.
body:
Many tanks and some pod devices include an airflow ring or slider. It looks minor, but it has a real effect on how your vape feels.

## What airflow does
Airflow sets how much air mixes with the vapor. Closing it restricts the draw and concentrates flavor. Opening it makes the draw easy and the vapor cooler and larger.

## Tight airflow
A tight draw is similar to drawing on a cigarette. It suits nicotine salts and mouth-to-lung style. Flavor is concentrated, and the throat feel is stronger.

## Open airflow
An open draw suits larger tanks and lower-strength liquid. The vapor is denser and cooler, and flavor is a little more diluted.

## How to find your setting
Start in the middle and move a quarter turn at a time. If the draw feels hot or harsh, open the airflow. If flavor is weak, close it a little. Take a few puffs at each change.

## Match with coil and liquid
Higher-resistance coils work with tight airflow; sub-ohm coils need more air. See [sub-ohm versus mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/). Liquids that are too thick can also cause gurgling when airflow is wrong; see [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/).

## Choosing hardware
If you enjoy tuning, pick a kit with adjustable airflow from our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Otherwise, a fixed-airflow pod is simpler. Adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Does airflow change nicotine intake?
faq.a: Airflow changes how much vapor and air you draw per puff, which can change how strong it feels. Strength itself is set by the liquid.

faq.q: Is a loose draw better?
faq.a: It is a preference. Some people prefer a loose, cool draw and others a tight one.

title: Choosing a Vape for Travel: Size, Leaks and Battery
summary: Traveling with a vape takes planning. Compare compact devices, leak resistance and battery options for trips and commutes.
body:
Whether you are commuting or flying, a travel-friendly vape is compact, leak-resistant and easy to charge. Here is what to look for.

## Choose a compact device
Slim pod systems and small disposables slip into a pocket. Large box mods are bulky and need more careful packing.

## Leak resistance matters
Pressure changes during a flight can push liquid out of a full pod or tank. Closed pods and disposables resist leaks better than open tanks. If you carry refillable gear, keep it nearly empty and sealed in a bag. Read our guide to [stopping a vape from leaking](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

## Battery and charging
A USB-C rechargeable device is the easiest to top up from a power bank or laptop. Always carry batteries in your hand luggage, not checked bags. Our [airline rules overview](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/) explains the basics.

## Pack spares sensibly
Take one spare pod and a short charging cable. For refills, use small bottles instead of a large one.

## Check local laws
Vape rules differ between states and countries. Some places ban use in public spaces or even possession. Always check the rules where you are going; see [state and local vape laws](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Where to shop
Browse compact [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) with travel in mind. Adults 21+ only, and keep products away from children.

faq.q: Can I vape on a plane?
faq.a: No. Vaping is prohibited on commercial flights, and devices must go in carry-on baggage.

faq.q: How do I stop leaks in my bag?
faq.a: Keep pods upright, nearly empty and in a sealed pouch, and avoid sudden pressure changes where possible.

title: Best Disposable Vapes for Flavor Lovers: How to Choose
summary: Want flavor above all? Here is how to choose a disposable by flavor family, cooling level and sweetness, and what to try first.

If flavor drives your choice, you can narrow hundreds of options with a few questions. Use this approach to find a device you will enjoy to the last puff.

## Pick a flavor family
Fruit is the largest group: berry blends, citrus, tropical and melon. Mint and menthol are crisp, dessert flavors lean creamy and sweet, and tobacco profiles lean earthy. Decide which family you naturally prefer.

## Decide on cooling
Names that include "ice" usually add a cooling effect. It can brighten fruit flavors, but too much can mute sweetness. Try a version with and without ice to learn your preference. Our list of [ice flavors](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/) goes deeper.

## Consider sweetness
Some recipes are very sweet, others tart or balanced. If you find sweet liquids heavy after a while, look for tart or mixed-fruit names with citrus.

## Mix and rotate
Many flavor fans keep two or three devices and rotate, which reduces taste fatigue. Check bulk and multi-pack offers in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/).

## Quality factors
A mesh coil, steady battery and well-balanced recipe all improve flavor. See [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/).

## Start small
Order one new flavor at a time before committing to a pack. Browse by taste in our flavor guides like [watermelon vapes](/blog/watermelon-vape-flavors-guide/) and [blue razz vapes](/blog/blue-razz-vape-flavors-guide/). Adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Why does flavor fade after a while?
faq.a: Taste fatigue is common, so rotating between flavors can help. A weakening coil can also dull flavor.

faq.q: Do sweeter flavors use more liquid?
faq.a: Not by themselves, but very sweet liquids can leave residue on the coil and shorten its life.

summary: New to vaping as an adult? Compare a first disposable, a pod kit and basic accessories, plus the mistakes that cost beginners money.

Starting as an adult can feel overwhelming. The market is crowded, but a few sensible choices keep it simple and affordable.

## Option 1: a disposable
The simplest start. No refilling, no coils and no setup. Choose one with a flavor you already like and a mid-range puff count. See [how to choose a disposable](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).

## Option 2: a pod kit
If you expect to use a vape regularly, a pod kit costs less over time. It needs a bit more learning, such as filling a pod and priming the coil. Our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) explains what to buy.

## Pick the right nicotine
Nicotine strength should match the device. Read our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/). Remember nicotine is addictive; if you do not already use nicotine, vaping is not recommended.

## Avoid these mistakes
- Buying the largest puff count right away.
- Using the wrong liquid thickness for your pod.
- Not charging a rechargeable device before first use.
- Keeping a vape in a hot car, which can harm the battery.

## Accessories worth having
A spare pod or coil and a USB-C cable are enough. Skip extras until you know what you like.

## Age and ID
You must be 21 or older, and delivery requires an adult signature with photo ID. See [age verification explained](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/). Browse our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) when ready.

faq.q: Is a disposable or a kit better for a beginner?
faq.a: A disposable is easier to start, while a kit is cheaper if you plan to vape regularly.

faq.q: How much should I spend to start?
faq.a: A disposable or basic pod kit in the $15 to $40 range is typical. Spending more is not required to begin.

The same token exists on several blockchains. We accept USDT on **Ethereum (ERC20)** and **Tron (TRC20)**. Each has its own wallet address, and you must send on the network you selected.

Tron transfers typically cost much less than Ethereum and settle quickly. For payments of a few hundred dollars, many people choose TRC20 to keep fees low. Your wallet or exchange must support Tron withdrawals.

Ethereum is the most widely supported network. Fees can be higher, especially when the network is busy, but compatibility is excellent.

- **Lowest fee:** TRC20.

- **Your balance is on one network:** use that one, and do not bridge just to pay.

Send on exactly the network shown in the payment window. A transfer on the wrong network will not arrive and may not be recoverable. Read [what to do after a wrong-network send](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/).

title: What Is a Crypto Network, and Why Does It Matter When You Pay?
summary: The same coin can live on several blockchains. Learn what a network is and why choosing the right one decides whether your payment arrives.
body:
When you pay with crypto you choose a coin and a network. The network is the blockchain that carries the transfer, and getting it right is the single most important step.

## Coin versus network
Bitcoin only lives on the Bitcoin network. But a stablecoin like USDT exists on several, including Ethereum and Tron. They are the same token, issued on different blockchains, each with its own address format and rules.

## Why a wrong network is a problem
An address on one network is not valid on another, even if it looks similar. Sending on the wrong network can mean the funds never reach us, and sometimes they cannot be recovered at all. Read [what to do after a wrong-network send](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/).

## How to spot the network
The payment window states the network next to the address, for example "Tron (TRC20)" or "Solana (SOL)". Exchanges show similar labels when you withdraw. Match them exactly.

## Address formats
- Bitcoin addresses start with bc1, 1 or 3.
- Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain addresses start with 0x.
- Tron addresses start with T.
- Solana addresses are long base58 strings.

## Fees vary by network
Some networks cost cents, others dollars. See [network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/) for details.

## Takeaway
Pick the network in our window, match it in your wallet, copy the address with the copy button and send. For a worked example, read [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I tell the network from the address?
faq.a: Often, yes. The first characters and length differ, but always rely on the network label in the payment window.

faq.q: Do exchanges list networks?
faq.a: Yes. When you withdraw, an exchange asks you to choose a network, and it must match ours.

title: How We Detect Your Crypto Payment Automatically
summary: After you press I have paid, we look for your transfer on the blockchain. Here is how matching works, what we check and when a human steps in.
body:
You should not have to wait for someone to read a screenshot. For most networks, we match payments to orders automatically.

## What happens when you press "I have paid"
Your order is created and you are taken to a status page. From there, our system reads public blockchain data for the shop wallet on the network you chose and looks for an incoming transfer that fits your order.

## What we check
- **Network and address:** the transfer must arrive at the right wallet on the right network.
- **Amount:** the USD value of the transfer must be close to your order total, with a small tolerance for market movement.
- **Time:** it must be recent, shortly before or after you placed the order.
- **Uniqueness:** a single transaction can pay only one order.

## States you may see
- **Waiting:** nothing matching yet.
- **Detected:** a transfer is visible but not fully confirmed.
- **Confirmed:** matched and confirmed; you get an email.
- **Underpaid:** we found a payment that is short of the total. See [why that happens](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## When a human steps in
On networks where automatic detection is not available, or when amounts do not match, a team member checks your screenshot and the transaction hash. You can add both on the status page; see [uploading a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/).

## Privacy
We only use public blockchain data and do not ask for private keys or seed phrases. Never share those with anyone.

## Ready to pay?

title: Crypto Network Fees Explained: Gas, Sats and Why They Vary
summary: Every crypto transfer pays a fee to the network, not to us. See how fees work on each chain and how to keep yours low.
body:
When you send crypto, you pay a network fee to the people or validators who process transactions. We do not receive or control it. Fees vary a lot depending on the chain and how busy it is.

## Bitcoin
Fees depend on the size of the transaction and network demand, measured in satoshis per byte. They can be small in quiet periods and higher when many people transact. Most wallets let you pick a speed.

## Ethereum
Fees are called gas and depend on demand. Token transfers such as USDT cost more than plain ETH. Busy times can make small payments expensive.

## Tron
Tron uses resources called bandwidth and energy. If you do not hold them, the network burns a small amount of TRX. Many exchanges simply charge a flat withdrawal fee.

## Solana
Fees are tiny, usually a fraction of a cent. Keep a small amount of SOL for fees even if you send USDC.

## BNB Smart Chain
Fees are low and paid in BNB.

## Ways to keep fees down
- Choose a network with cheap fees, such as TRC20 or Solana.
- Avoid peak times on Ethereum.
- On exchanges, compare withdrawal fees between networks.

## Fees and the amount we receive
Make sure the amount arriving equals the amount in our window. Some exchanges deduct their fee from your withdrawal, so add it on top. See [sending from an exchange](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/).

## Next steps

faq.a: No. We offer a discount for crypto. Network and exchange fees go to the network and your provider.

faq.a: Demand for block space is high, and fees rise with demand.

title: Sent Crypto on the Wrong Network? What to Do Next
summary: Mistakes happen. If you used the wrong network or address, here are the steps to take immediately and what is realistically recoverable.
body:
Sending crypto on the wrong network is one of the most common mistakes. Do not panic, but do not send more funds either.

## Stop and gather details
Collect the transaction hash, the coin, the network you used, the amount and the time. Take screenshots of the exchange or wallet confirmation.

## Understand what happened
There are a few cases:
- **Right coin, wrong network, address compatible:** on some EVM networks the same address works on several chains. The funds may be sitting at that address on the other chain.
- **Address format incompatible:** the transaction usually fails or is blocked by the exchange before it leaves.
- **Sent to an address we do not control:** unrecoverable by anyone.

## Contact us right away
Use the [contact page](/contact/) or WhatsApp with your order reference and the details above. We will check what arrived and tell you honestly whether anything can be done. We cannot promise recovery, as it depends on whether we control the receiving address on that chain.

## Contact the sender's provider too
If you used an exchange, open a support ticket. Some can help with wrong-network deposits in limited cases.

## Do not resend yet
Wait until we confirm. Resending without checking can double the problem.

## Avoiding it next time
Match the network label in the payment window, use copy buttons and read [what a crypto network is](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/). To reduce the chance of an error with stablecoins, see [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.a: No. Recovery is only possible in limited situations and depends on the network and address.

title: Why Your Crypto Payment Shows Underpaid (and How to Fix It)
summary: Seen an underpaid message? Price movement, fees deducted by an exchange or a typo can leave a payment short. Here is how to resolve it.
body:
An underpaid status means we found a transfer that is smaller than your order total. It is usually easy to fix.

## Common causes
- **Exchange fee deducted:** some exchanges subtract their withdrawal fee from the amount, so less arrives than you entered.
- **Price movement:** a volatile coin can drop between the quote and your transfer.
- **Rounding or a typo:** a missing digit in the amount.
- **Partial payment:** you meant to pay in two parts.

## How we decide
We compare the dollar value of the received transfer to your order total, allowing a small tolerance for normal movement. Anything clearly short is marked underpaid, and the status page shows the amount we received.

## How to fix it
1. Check the received amount on your status page.
2. Send the missing balance to the same address and network.
3. Press "I have paid" or upload the second transaction hash.
4. If you are unsure, contact us from the [contact page](/contact/) with your order reference.

## Avoiding it
Use stablecoins such as [USDT](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/) or [USDC](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/) for exact amounts, add the exchange withdrawal fee on top, and send soon after the quote loads. Read [network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/).

## Overpaid?
If you sent more than needed, tell us. We will review it and let you know how it can be handled.

## Related

faq.a: A small percentage for volatile coins and tighter for stablecoins. Anything clearly short is flagged.

faq.a: No. Only the missing balance is needed.

Crypto on a fast network can be confirmed within minutes, and detection is automatic on most networks. Gift cards depend on you buying the card and uploading the details, then us verifying them. Typically crypto is quicker once you hold coins.

If you have never used crypto, setting up a wallet or exchange takes time. Gift cards can be bought in minutes from a familiar site. See [how gift card payment works](/blog/how-gift-card-payment-works/) and [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/).

Crypto has network fees and exchange fees. Gift cards usually have no extra fee beyond the card price, though some retailers add small charges. Compare the total against the 10% saving.

Stablecoins like [USDT](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/) let you send exact amounts. Gift cards come in set amounts, so you may need to round up.

## Reversibility
Crypto transfers are final. Gift cards are also hard to recover once the code is sent. Be careful in both cases.

- **Already hold crypto:** use crypto.
- **Prefer a familiar checkout:** use a gift card.
- **Want exact amounts:** use stablecoins.

If you pay with crypto or a gift card, you get 10% off the product subtotal, and the free-shipping check is applied after that discount. title: Order Status Meanings: Awaiting Payment, Proof Submitted and More
summary: Confused by an order status? This glossary explains each stage, what we are doing and what you may need to do next.
body:
Your private order page shows a status. Each one tells you what is happening and what, if anything, you should do.

## Awaiting payment
We have your order but no confirmed payment. For crypto, make or complete the transfer. For Cash App, Apple Pay and Chime, watch for our details. For gift cards, buy the card and upload it.

## Payment details sent
We emailed or messaged you the details. Pay the exact amount and upload your receipt.

## Proof submitted
You uploaded a screenshot, hash or gift card details. A team member is reviewing it, normally within business hours.

## Payment detected on-chain
For crypto, a transfer is visible on the network but not fully confirmed yet. No action is needed unless it stays that way for a long time.

## Payment confirmed
We have confirmed your payment, and your order enters processing. You receive an email.

## Shipped
Your package is on its way. A tracking email follows. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## Cancelled
The order was cancelled, for example if payment was not received in time.

## What to do if stuck
If an order sits in one status longer than expected, contact us from the [contact page](/contact/) with your ID. Read [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/) for the typical timeline.

## Related
Learn about [uploading proof](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.a: If payment is not received within the period stated in the payment terms, the order may be released.

title: What to Do If Your Package Is Delayed
summary: Late parcels happen. Follow this checklist to find out where yours is and when to contact us for help.
body:
If your order has not arrived when you expected, work through these steps.

## 1. Check the timeline
Add our processing time (24 to 72 business hours) to the carrier transit estimate for your region. Weekends and federal holidays do not count. West Coast deliveries take about 3 to 7 business days in transit, and the eastern half of the US about 11 to 18. See [shipping times](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## 2. Look at tracking
Open your tracking email or the order page. Updates can pause for several days in regional carrier networks. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## 3. Look for a delivery notice
Because an adult must sign, carriers often leave a note after a missed attempt. Check your door, mailbox and phone.

## 4. Confirm your address
Make sure the address on your order is correct, including apartment numbers.

## 5. Contact the carrier
If tracking shows delivered but you do not have it, call the carrier with your tracking number.

## 6. Contact us
If the estimated window has passed, email or WhatsApp us with your order ID. Business contact options are on the [contact page](/contact/).

## Returned packages
If a carrier returns an undelivered package, a refund is available minus the restocking fee and shipping cost, per the [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Lost or damaged
For damage see [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

Returns and exchanges must be requested within 30 days of the purchase date.

Contact us before sending anything back so we can issue an RMA form. Returns without an RMA cannot be guaranteed a refund or exchange. Use the [contact page](/contact/) to begin.

After we receive the product, we issue a refund minus a 15% restocking fee. Shipping fees are not refunded, and you are responsible for return shipping. We do not provide prepaid return labels and recommend adding insurance.

- Opened or used e-liquid.

- Items not bought from our store.

- Puffco products, which do not qualify for refunds or exchanges.

## Returned by the carrier
If a carrier returns an undelivered package, refund rules in the [shipping policy](/shipping/) apply.

Add gate codes, buzzer numbers and building notes in the order notes. Tell your building staff to expect a delivery that needs a signature.

Carriers cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box. Use a street address.

Use the name on your ID. Some carriers require the recipient's name to match.

Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands and military addresses are excluded from free shipping, and we do not ship internationally. See [where we ship](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

Buying for anyone under 21 is illegal. Keep products out of reach of children; see [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/).

title: The PACT Act Explained for Vape Buyers
summary: The PACT Act changed how vape products are shipped, taxed and delivered. Here is a plain summary of what it means for online buyers.
body:
The Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking (PACT) Act was amended by legislation signed in December 2020. Its provisions covering e-cigarettes and vaping products took effect on March 27, 2021. This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## What it covers
The law treats vaping products similarly to cigarettes for remote sales. That includes how they are shipped, taxed and delivered.

## Shipping limits
The U.S. Postal Service may not carry vaping products, so sellers use other carriers. Some carriers have also limited what they accept, which can lead to interruptions in some areas.

## Adult signature
Every delivery must be signed for by an adult aged 21 or older with ID. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).

## Labeling
Parcels must carry a label stating that federal law requires payment of applicable excise taxes and compliance with licensing and tax-stamping obligations.

## Taxes and licensing
Sellers must register and comply with state and local licensing and tax rules. Some states tax vape products and sellers may collect those taxes. See [vape taxes overview](/blog/vape-taxes-by-state-overview/).

## What it means for you
You may see delivery rules and restrictions that did not exist for older orders. Our own summary is on the [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/) page, and details on shipping are in the [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Not legal advice
Rules change, so confirm requirements with official sources. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is online vape shopping legal?
faq.a: Remote sales are allowed under federal law when sellers comply with the PACT Act and with state and local rules.

faq.q: Why can no one ship by USPS?
faq.a: The PACT Act prohibits the Postal Service from carrying vaping products.

title: The FDA and Vaping Products: What Adult Buyers Should Know
summary: The FDA regulates e-cigarettes as tobacco products. Learn what marketing authorization means and why you should check product and local rules.
body:
In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulates e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems as tobacco products. This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## Marketing authorization
New tobacco products generally need FDA marketing authorization before they can be legally sold. Only some vaping products have received it. Many products on the market have not, and enforcement actions against unauthorized products can change what retailers may sell.

## What this means for buyers
Availability can change quickly. Products you could buy last year may become restricted, and some states restrict sales to authorized products only. Check your local rules before you order.

## Warning statements
Packaging must carry the FDA nicotine warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." See [what the warning means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## No health claims
We make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims about any product, and you should be cautious of any seller that does.

## Our disclaimer
Our [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/) page explains our position in detail. If you have questions about a specific product, ask us via the [contact page](/contact/).

## How to stay informed
Visit the FDA's tobacco products pages and your state's regulator for current lists and rules. Also read [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Browse responsibly
Adults 21+ only. See [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) when you are ready.

faq.q: Does FDA regulation mean a product is approved?
faq.a: No. Regulation is not an endorsement, and authorization applies only to specific products that received it.

faq.q: Where can I check the status?
faq.a: The FDA publishes information on authorized tobacco products on its website.

title: Vape Taxes by State: A Plain Overview
summary: Many states tax vaping products, using different methods and rates. Here is how those taxes generally work and why they affect online orders.
body:
If your state taxes vaping products, it can change what you pay. This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## Why states tax vapes
Many states levy excise taxes on e-cigarettes and e-liquids, similar to those on cigarettes. The goal is often revenue and discouraging use.

## How taxes are calculated
Methods differ:
- **Percentage of price:** a share of the wholesale or retail price.
- **Per milliliter:** a fixed amount per mL of liquid.
- **Per device or per cartridge:** a flat amount per item.
- **Mixed systems:** a combination.

## Online sales and the PACT Act
Under the PACT Act, remote sellers must comply with state tax requirements, and in some cases collect and remit them. See the [PACT Act overview](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/).

## Seeing it on your order
Where applicable, taxes are itemized in your order total. Free-shipping thresholds are measured before tax. See [minimum order and free shipping](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/).

## Where to get exact numbers
Rates change often. Check your state's department of revenue or taxation website for current rules.

## Impact on prices
Tax can raise the cost of a vape noticeably in some states. Compare overall costs with [cost per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/).

## Questions
Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your state and we will explain how it appears on your order. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Do all states tax vapes?
faq.a: No. Many do, but the methods and rates differ, and some do not.

faq.a: Not usually. Where applicable it is added and itemized.

title: Traveling With Vapes: Airline and Battery Rules in Brief
summary: Vapes belong in carry-on bags, never checked luggage, and cannot be used on board. Learn the basics before your next trip.
body:
If you are flying with a vape, a few rules apply almost everywhere. This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## Carry-on only
Under U.S. aviation rules, e-cigarettes, vaporizers and spare lithium batteries must travel in carry-on baggage. They are not allowed in checked bags, because battery fires are easier to handle in the cabin.

## No vaping on board
Using a vape on a commercial aircraft, including in the lavatory, is prohibited.

## Protect batteries
Keep spare batteries in a case or separate pouches so metal objects cannot touch the terminals. Switch off devices, lock the fire button if it has one and store them where they cannot be pressed accidentally.

## Liquids
Liquids follow the standard carry-on liquid rules: containers of 3.4 ounces or less in a clear bag. Pressure changes can cause leaks, so keep pods nearly empty and sealed. See [choosing a vape for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/).

## At your destination
Rules differ by state, city and country. Some places ban vape use in public or even possession. Read [state and local vape laws](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## International travel
Many countries restrict or ban vapes and nicotine liquids. Check the laws and customs rules before you go.

## Related
Check [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/). Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I put my vape in checked luggage?
faq.a: No. Vapes and spare lithium batteries belong in carry-on bags.

faq.q: Can I vape in an airport?
faq.a: Only where it is allowed. Many airports restrict it to certain areas or ban it entirely.

title: Lithium Battery Care Basics for Vape Devices
summary: Most vapes use lithium-ion batteries. Follow these care basics to protect the device, avoid damage and extend battery life.
body:
Almost every rechargeable vape uses a lithium-ion battery. Treat it with the same care as a phone or power bank.

## Use the right charger
Charge with the cable supplied or a reputable one, from a standard USB port or wall adapter. Cheap, unbranded chargers can supply inconsistent power.

## Do not leave it charging unattended
Charge on a hard, flat, non-flammable surface and avoid sleeping with a charging device by your bed.

## Avoid heat and cold
Do not leave a vape in a hot car or direct sun, and avoid freezing temperatures. Heat shortens battery life and can damage the device.

## Do not use a damaged device
Stop using any device that is swollen, dented, hot to touch, leaking or has damaged wiring. Dispose of it properly; see [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Pocket and bag habits
Keep devices separate from coins and keys, which can short the battery terminals. Use a case if possible.

## Replaceable batteries
Box mods that use removable cells need correctly rated batteries. Never mix brands, ages or charge levels, and use cells with wraps in good condition.

## Charging habits
Charge before the device is completely empty when you can, and unplug once it is full. See [extending battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/) and [charging a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/).

## Where to shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I use a phone fast charger?
faq.a: Many devices tolerate it, but check the manual. If unsure, use a standard 5V adapter.

faq.q: How long do vape batteries last?
faq.a: Built-in batteries typically last for hundreds of charge cycles, depending on use and care.

title: How to Dispose of Vapes, Pods and Batteries Responsibly
summary: Vapes contain batteries, electronics and residual nicotine. Here is how to dispose of them properly and where to look for recycling options.
body:
A used vape is not ordinary trash. It contains a lithium battery, electronics, plastics and residual liquid containing nicotine.

## Why it matters
Lithium batteries can start fires in garbage trucks and recycling plants when crushed. Nicotine liquid is hazardous to children, pets and the environment if it leaks.

## Do not put them in household trash or curbside recycling
Many municipalities treat vapes as electronic or hazardous waste. Check your local rules.

## Where to take them
- **Household hazardous waste sites** and collection events.
- **Electronics recycling programs** that accept small electronics.
- **Battery drop-off locations** at some retailers, which may accept lithium batteries.
Search for your city's hazardous waste page or use a recycling locator.

## Before you drop it off
Stop using any damaged or swollen device. Put it in a sealed plastic bag, tape over battery terminals if exposed, and keep it away from heat. Do not try to open or crush it.

## Liquids
Do not pour leftover liquid down the drain. Absorb small amounts with cat litter or paper towels, seal in a bag and take it to hazardous waste, following local guidance.

## Pods and coils
Used pods and coils go in the same stream as the device, unless your local program says otherwise.

## Related
Learn about [battery care](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/) and [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I throw a dead disposable in the trash?
faq.a: Check local rules. Most areas ask you to treat it as electronic or hazardous waste because of the lithium battery.

faq.q: Does a dead vape still contain nicotine?
faq.a: It may contain residual liquid, so keep it away from children and pets until disposed of.

title: Keeping Vapes and E-Liquid Away From Children and Pets
summary: Nicotine liquid and devices must be kept out of reach. Here is how adults can store them responsibly and what to do if there is a spill.
body:
E-liquid contains nicotine, and a small amount can be dangerous to children and pets. Responsible storage is part of being an adult user.

## Store out of reach and out of sight
Keep liquids, pods and devices in a high, closed cabinet or a lockable box. Do not leave them on tables, in handbags or in cars.

## Keep original packaging
Child-resistant caps and warning labels are on the packaging for a reason. Do not decant liquid into unlabelled or food-style containers.

## Do not use food-style containers
Brightly colored or fruit-flavored liquid can attract attention. Never store it in drink bottles or near snacks.

## Handle spills promptly
Wipe spills with paper towels while wearing gloves, wash the surface and your hands, and dispose of the towels responsibly. Avoid skin contact.

## If someone is exposed
Contact Poison Control right away at 1-800-222-1222 in the U.S., or your local emergency number. Do not wait for symptoms.

## Dispose responsibly
Used devices and empty pods are also hazardous. See [how to dispose of vapes](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Everyday habits
Charge devices where children cannot reach them, and never let anyone under 21 handle a vape. Read about [age verification](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/) and [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/).

## Browse
See [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is vape liquid dangerous if swallowed?
faq.a: Yes. Nicotine liquid can be harmful if swallowed or absorbed through skin, so seek help immediately.

faq.q: Who do I call?
faq.a: Poison Control in the U.S. at 1-800-222-1222, or emergency services in an emergency.

title: What the Nicotine Warning Label Means
summary: Every nicotine product carries a warning. Here is what the statement says, why it is required and how to read it as an adult consumer.
body:
Look at any vape, e-liquid or pouch sold in the United States and you will find a warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## Why the warning exists
The FDA requires it on the packaging and in advertisements for nicotine products. It reminds adults that nicotine is addictive.

## What it tells you
Nicotine is a stimulant that the body can become dependent on. Using a product that contains it can lead to cravings and dependence, which is why products are limited to adults aged 21 and over.

## Where to find it
On the front or side panel of the package, often in a bordered box. If a product has no warning, treat it with caution and do not buy it.

## What it does not say
It does not describe a product as more or less harmful than any other. We do not make health comparisons, and neither should sellers.

## Other warnings
You may see notes for pregnant or nursing women, people with health conditions and children and pets. Follow them. Nothing here is medical advice; consult a healthcare professional with questions.

title: How Does a Vape Work? Battery, Coil, Wick and Liquid
summary: A vape is a battery that heats a coil to turn liquid into vapor. Here is how each part works together in plain language.
body:
Every vape, from a tiny disposable to a large box mod, works on the same basic principle: a battery powers a small heater that turns liquid into an inhalable vapor.

## The four key parts
- **Battery:** supplies power to the heater.
- **Coil:** a small heating element, made from wire or mesh.
- **Wick:** usually cotton, it soaks up liquid and holds it against the coil.
- **E-liquid:** a mixture of propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin, flavoring and usually nicotine.

## What happens when you inhale
When you draw on the mouthpiece, an airflow sensor detects the change and sends power to the coil, or you press a button. The coil heats up in a fraction of a second. The liquid in the wick vaporizes, and the vapor travels through the airflow path to your mouth.

## Why liquid and airflow must balance
If the wick is dry, the coil can scorch the cotton and taste burnt. If there is too much liquid, it can flood and gurgle. See [fixing gurgling](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/) and [a burnt taste](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## Device types
Disposables are sealed units; pods have a replaceable pod; box mods use tanks with replaceable coils. Compare them in [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/).

## Nicotine and flavor
Nicotine strength and type are set by the liquid, while flavor comes from the recipe. Learn about [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Safety reminder
Nicotine is addictive and these products are for adults 21+. See [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) for starter hardware.

faq.q: Is vapor the same as smoke?
faq.a: No. Vapor is created by heating liquid, not by burning plant material. We make no health claims either way.

faq.q: Why does a coil need to be primed?
faq.a: A dry wick can burn. Soaking it first prevents a burnt taste.

The heating element, usually mesh or wire. It wears out and needs replacing. Learn [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/).

Cotton inside the coil that carries liquid to the heating surface.

## Battery
Powers the heater. Capacity is measured in mAh. See [battery basics](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/).

## Airflow control
A ring or slider that adjusts air intake. See [adjustable airflow](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## 510 connector
A standard threaded connection that lets many tanks fit many mods.

## Charging port
Modern devices use USB-C. Older devices use micro-USB or proprietary connectors.

## Fire button and sensor
Devices fire on inhale (auto-draw) or when you press a button.

## Shopping
Match replacement parts to your exact device. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Adults 21+ only.

title: Vape Glossary: Common Terms Every Shopper Should Know
summary: Understand the jargon on product pages, from MTL and DTL to mAh, ohm, shortfill and nic salts, all in one quick reference.
body:
Product pages use a lot of shorthand. Here are the terms you will meet most often.

## Device terms
- **Disposable:** a pre-filled, ready-to-use device. See [how to choose one](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).
- **Pod:** a compact, replaceable liquid cartridge.
- **Mod:** a battery unit, often with adjustable power.
- **Tank:** a refillable container with a coil.

## Electrical terms
- **mAh:** battery capacity, in milliamp hours.
- **Ohm (Ω):** coil resistance.
- **Watt (W):** power delivered to the coil.

## Style terms
- **MTL:** mouth-to-lung inhale.
- **DTL / sub-ohm:** direct-to-lung inhale with a low-resistance coil. See [the difference](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/).

## Liquid terms
- **PG / VG:** propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin, the liquid base. See [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).
- **Nic salts:** a smoother type of nicotine for low-power devices.
- **Freebase:** the traditional form of nicotine.
- **Shortfill:** a bottle with spare room for nicotine shots.
- **Steeping:** letting liquid rest so flavors blend.

## Experience terms
- **Throat hit:** the sensation of vapor on the throat.
- **Ghosting:** a lingering flavor from a previous liquid.
- **Dry hit:** a harsh, burnt draw from a dry wick.

## Brand terms
- **Puffs:** the estimated number of draws; see [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/).

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: What does MTL mean?
faq.a: Mouth-to-lung, a draw style where vapor is held in the mouth before inhaling.

faq.q: What is ghosting?
faq.a: Flavor from a previous liquid lingering in the coil or wick.

title: mAh, Puffs and Battery Life: How They Relate
summary: A bigger battery does not always mean more puffs. See how mAh, power mode and coil design combine to decide how long a vape lasts.
body:
Battery capacity, measured in milliamp hours (mAh), is just one factor in how long a vape runs. Here is how the pieces fit.

## What mAh tells you
mAh measures how much charge a battery holds. A 1,000 mAh battery holds twice the charge of a 500 mAh one, all else equal.

## Power use matters
A device that runs at low power uses less energy per puff than a high-wattage one. Boost modes drain the battery faster. So a smaller battery on an efficient device can last as long as a bigger one on a power-hungry device.

## Puff counts and batteries
Puff counts on disposables are set mostly by liquid volume, with the battery sized to match. See [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/). Rechargeable models can add extra puffs by charging.

## Real-world factors
- Draw length and frequency.
- Temperature: batteries lose capacity when cold.
- Age: capacity falls after many cycles.
- Coil resistance.

## Reading product pages
Look for mAh and for any mention of USB-C charging or pass-through. Our [rechargeable versus non-rechargeable article](/blog/rechargeable-vs-non-rechargeable-disposables/) shows what to check.

## Looking after it
Care extends life: see [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/) and [extending battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/).

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is more mAh always better?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Capacity helps, but efficiency and usage patterns matter too.

faq.q: Why does my battery die faster in winter?
faq.a: Cold temperatures reduce a lithium battery's effective capacity.

title: What Is a Mesh Coil, and Why Do So Many Vapes Use One?
summary: Mesh coils use a thin metal sheet instead of a wire wrap. Learn how that changes heating, flavor and why it became popular.
body:
If you have shopped for vapes recently, you have seen "mesh coil" on almost every listing. Here is what it means.

## From wire to mesh
Traditional coils wrap a wire around a cotton wick. A mesh coil replaces the wire with a thin sheet of woven or perforated metal that lines the wick.

## Why it heats differently
A mesh sheet has a large surface area touching the cotton. That means liquid is heated across a wide area rather than in a few hot spots. The result is quicker heating and more even vaporization.

## What users notice
- Smoother, fuller flavor.
- Consistent vapor from puff to puff.
- Less chance of local scorching.

## Coils in disposables
Most modern disposables use mesh coils to deliver consistent flavor for thousands of puffs. Dual-mesh designs double down on this. See [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/).

## Drawbacks
Mesh coils can cost more to make and can be affected by thick or sweet liquids, which leave residue. Using the recommended liquid and power helps.

## Replacing them
Mesh coils still wear out. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and [picking replacements](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/).

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Is mesh better than wire?
faq.a: Mesh tends to give smoother flavor and heating, but a well-made wire coil can also perform well.

faq.q: Do mesh coils need priming?
faq.a: Yes. Let them soak before the first puff to avoid scorching.
